header: beside the paragraph that says what it means
bodytext:
The figure keeps the display size it would have on its own, and the rich-text column beside it does the work a caption cannot: what was counted, against what reference, and where the claim stops holding.

The toggle swaps the two halves. The figure still comes first in the source order either way, so a reader who never sees the layout meets the claim before the explanation of it.
note: The source line sits under a rule at the foot of the prose column. Put the method and the measurement date in it — an interpreted figure with no provenance is an assertion.
